response: The clustering still lacks a dedicated solar and stellar astrophysics cluster — papers on stellar evolution, stellar atmospheres, solar physics, and stellar rotation are scattered across multiple clusters and must be pulled together into one. The "High-Energy Astrophysics Phenomena" cluster is mixing in solar wind heating, electron temperature diagnostics in nebulae, and nucleosynthesis topics that belong in solar/stellar or galactic/extragalactic instead. The "Galaxies Stellar Populations Dynamics" cluster contains planet formation and protoplanetary disk papers that should be in the planetary/exoplanet cluster. The goal remains exactly six clusters: galactic/extragalactic, solar/stellar, cosmology/LSS, planetary/exoplanets, high-energy, and instrumentation/methods — with every paper placed by its primary subject area and no miscellaneous bins.
